title: Splitting a nodal curve point over a finite separable field extension
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $C$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Assume that for every algebraically closed extension $\Omega/k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], $C_\Omega=C\times_k\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ [def-pc-base-change] is empty or equidimensional of dimension $1$ [def-weil-pure-dimension], and at every nonsmooth point [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] its maximal-ideal-adic completed local ring [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] is $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. For every point $x\in C$ at which $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is not smooth, $x$ is closed [def-weil-closed-points], $\kappa(x)/k$ is finite separable [def-weil-residue-field] [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], and there is a finite separable field extension $k'/k$ [def-pc-field-extension] containing a chosen copy of $\kappa(x)$, with $[k':\kappa(x)]\leq2$, and a $k'$-rational point $x'\in C_{k'}$ above $x$ such that $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{C_{k'},x'}\cong k'[[u,v]]/(uv)$ as $k'$-algebras. Here $k'$-rational means that the induced residue-field map $k'\to\kappa(x')$ is an isomorphism; the last condition is called a split node.

source.place: Tags 0CBT (remark-quadratic-extension), 0CBU (remark-trivial-quadratic-extension), 0CBW (lemma-split-node); applied to the nodal points characterized by lemma-nodal, as in the residue-field paragraph of lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-geometric-node-residue-rationalization] to $C,x$. It gives closedness of $x$, finite separability of $F=\kappa(x)$ over $k$, and the canonical closed $F$-rational point $z$ of $D=C_F$ over $x$. It also gives that $D$ is finite type of dimension one and that the lift of $z$ to an algebraic closure of $F$ has completed local ring $\overline F[[u,v]]/(uv)$.

source.place: Tag 0CBY (lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family), first proof, residue-field paragraph, expanded through Tag 0C59 (lemma-nodal-family) and Morphisms Tag 02G7 (morphisms.tex, lemma-unramified-over-field). The dimension check is the affine base-change argument of the returned item, steps 1-4.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-rational-node-quadratic-completion] to $D,z$ over $F$. All its hypotheses are the conclusions of step 1. Obtain $a,b,c\in F$ with $b^2-4ac\ne0$ and an $F$-algebra isomorphism $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{D,z}\cong F[[u,v]]/(au^2+buv+cv^2)$. The $F$-algebra structure is the structural one, since $z$ is $F$-rational.

source.place: Tags 0C4D (lemma-nodal) and 0C49 (lemma-nodal-algebraic), residue field equal to F

proof.text: Choose an affine neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}S$ of $z$ with $S$ finitely generated over $F$, using [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Its evaluation map $\varepsilon:S\to F$ is an $F$-algebra map and is onto, since constants map identically to $F$; its maximal kernel $\mathfrak p$ represents $z$ and $S_{\mathfrak p}=\mathcal O_{D,z}$. Apply [lem-trf-quadratic-completion-separable-splitting] to this evaluation and the presentation from step 2. It gives $K/F$ finite separable of degree at most two. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], the kernel of $S\otimes_FK\to K$ is a point $x'$ of $D_K$ above $z$. The new node gives its local ring residue field $K$, with the structural residue map an isomorphism, and its completed local $K$-algebra $K[[U,V]]/(UV)$.

source.place: Tags 0CBT (remark-quadratic-extension) and 0CBU (remark-trivial-quadratic-extension), quadratic splitting and split completed equation; Varieties Tag 0C54 (varieties.tex, lemma-base-change-complete-local-ring), completed presentation after field extension. This is the explicit affine quadratic argument of the returned item, steps 6-8, before the final field-tower assembly.

proof.text: Under the iterated base-change identification $D_K=(C_F)_K=C_K$ of [def-pc-base-change], $x'$ lies over $x$. Apply [lem-zl-separable-permanence] to $k\subseteq F\subseteq K$ to obtain separability of $K/k$. If $(e_i)$ is a finite $k$-basis of $F$ and $(d_j)$ a finite $F$-basis of $K$, expanding the coefficients in $\sum_j\alpha_jd_j$ shows that the finitely many products $e_id_j$ span $K$ over $k$. Thus $K/k$ is finite. Take $k'=K$ with the chosen embedding $\kappa(x)=F\hookrightarrow K$; step 3 gives $[k':\kappa(x)]\le2$, rationality and the required split completion.
